  <section v="12">

    <t s="1">that the reason why the analogy of cause and effect is brought before the analogy of light and luminary,</t>
    <t s="2">is,</t>
    <t s="3">because the main innovation in this—that the creations that are brought into being from the name Havayah are nullified to Havayah—</t>

    <t s="5">that although they are creations</t>

    <t s="7">nevertheless the light of the name Havayah is felt in them in revelation,</t>

    <t s="9">However, in order to explain that the revelation of the source also exists in something that is incomparable to the source,</t>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The analogy of light and luminary is insufficient because in that analogy the light has no independent existence, whereas in the analogue, creation from the name Havayah brings about a new entity, not just a revelation.

translations.translation: However, the analogy of light and luminary is also insufficient,
for in light and luminary,
the closeness of the light to the luminary and its nullification to it is in a manner that the light is not an existence at all, and its entire essence is that it is a revelation of the luminary.
Not so in the analogue,
even in the bringing into being from the name Havayah, of which it is written "for He commanded and they were created,"
for the matter of creation is
(not an extension and revelation of the source,
but rather)
the bringing into being of a thing.
And this is also understood from what is said in Tanya51,
that even if the bringing into being were from the name Havayah without the tzimtzum of the name Elokim, the creations would be brought into being from nothing to something
(except that then they would be utterly nullified,
like the nullification of the sun's ray in the sun).
And in order to explain that even the existence of a thing is in closeness to its source,
this is through the analogy of cause and effect.
For although the effect is an existence and not a revelation of the cause, nevertheless it is in closeness to the cause.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The reason the analogy of cause and effect is brought before that of light and luminary is that the main innovation—that creations from Havayah are nullified to Him—is understood specifically from cause and effect, while light and luminary explains revelation of the source in something incomparable.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that the reason why the analogy of cause and effect is brought before the analogy of light and luminary,
is,
because the main innovation in this—that the creations that are brought into being from the name Havayah are nullified to Havayah—
is,
that although they are creations
(the existence of a thing),
nevertheless the light of the name Havayah is felt in them in revelation,
and this matter is understood specifically from the analogy of cause and effect.
However, in order to explain that the revelation of the source also exists in something that is incomparable to the source,
they add the analogy of light and luminary.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The world is defined by space and time because it is brought into being through the name Elokim, yet in the Holy Temple the unity of Havayah and Elokim was manifest, raising the question of why creation from Havayah alone would not still entail limitation.

translations.translation: And it is known52
that the fact that the world is defined by the categories of space and time is because its bringing into being is through the name Elokim,
and if it were brought into being from the name Havayah
(was, is, and will be as one53),
it would not be defined by the categories of space and time.
And this is why regarding the Holy Temple it is written "Indeed, Havayah is in this place,"
for54
in the Holy Temple, the place was above the category of place,
the place of the Ark is not from the measurement55.
However, the revelation that shone in the Holy Temple was the revelation of the name Havayah as it shines within the name Elokim.
For the name Havayah as it is in itself is above the category of place,
and this that the Holy of Holies was a measured and bounded place
(twenty cubits by twenty cubits),
and also the Ark was in the measurement of place
(two and a half cubits its length and a cubit and a half its width),
and nevertheless the place of the Ark is not from the measurement,
this is the matter of the unification of Havayah and Elokim56.
And it needs to be understood,
that since even in the bringing into being from the name Havayah, a new thing is brought into being that is not comparable to the source that brings it into being
[and the revelation of the name Havayah in the world that is brought into being from it is only in the matter of nullification,
that it is felt in them that their existence is only that the Divine light brings them into being every moment]57,
then even in the world as it is brought into being from the name Havayah, there would seemingly need to be the limitation of time and place.
